title: Matrix product verification run distribution
statement: For a natural number $n$, a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and matrices $A,B,C\in\mathbb F_2^{n\times n}$, the verification program’s run law is that of a uniformly random bit vector $b\in\{0,1\}^n$, paired with the decision whether $Cx= A(Bx)$ for every coordinate, where $x$ is the vector in $\mathbb F_2^n$ corresponding to $b$. The cost is $(0,0,n+6n^2+4n+1)$; it does not depend on $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Matrices $A,B,C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ of size $n\times n$
